look_here_first: Start with a mature capsule: the leathery surface is usually short-prickly or warty. On a flower, check whether stamens project conspicuously beyond petals (about twice petal length). Opposite palmately compound leaves establish buckeye, but do not separate Aesculus species.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous small to medium tree with stout twigs and large terminal buds.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, palmately compound, usually 5–7 serrate leaflets; leaves alone overlap A. pavia.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Terminal erect panicles; stamens markedly exserted, approximately twice petal length. Petals often pale green-yellow, but color is secondary.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Leathery round capsules usually short-spiny or warty (occasionally nearly smooth), with glossy brown seeds and pale hilum.
